title: Ceramics and Nano-Materials
welcome_lead: From alumina cutting tools to carbon nanotubes.
meta_desc: A-Level D&T: technical ceramics and nano-materials.

concepts.def: Engineering ceramic: high hardness, high temperature, brittle.
Aluminium oxide — cutting tool inserts, dental implants.
Toughened ceramic — dental crowns, knife blades.
Material with structural features below 100 nm.
Cylindrical carbon nano-structure, very high tensile strength.
Single-atom-thick sheet of carbon — Nobel Prize 2010 (Geim, Novoselov).

walkthroughs.body_html: Alumina and zirconia have hardness up to 1500 HV and operating temperatures above 1000 °C. They serve as cutting tools, prosthetic joints, and turbine blades.
Single-wall carbon nanotubes have tensile strength up to ~63 GPa — about 50 times steel. They reinforce polymer composites in aerospace and battery electrodes.
Graphene — first isolated by Geim and Novoselov at Manchester in 2004 (Nobel Prize 2010) — is a single-atom layer of graphite, with extraordinary strength and electrical conductivity.

mcqs.q: Carbon nanotubes are about how many times stronger than steel by tensile strength?

numericals.q: If a cutting tool has hardness 1500 HV and tool steel has 800 HV, what is the ratio (rounded to 1 dp)?
